title: What does ffmpeg do with GIF frame delays?
fullTitle: GIF to MP4: Delay 3 Is 33.33 fps, -r 30 Adds 11% to the Length, fps=30 Drops 2 Frames

scenes.narration: A gif stores one delay for every frame, in hundredths of a second. When ffmpeg writes an mp4, what happens to those delays?
captions: A gif stores a delay per frame, in hundredths of a second.
What happens to the delays in an mp4?

scenes.narration: Four panels. Twenty frames, each held three hundredths: point six seconds. Convert, and the projector runs at thirty three point three three frames a second. Say dash r thirty: it slows, and the clip lasts point six six seven. Say f p s equals thirty: the length stays, two frames vanish.
captions: -r 30: 0.667 s. fps=30: 0.6 s, two frames gone.

scenes.narration: We write the gifs byte by byte in Node: twenty frames, each numbered in six blocks. Delays two, three, four, six, ten, and a mix. Readers: delay bytes, f f probe, decoded pixels. Control: in the gif itself, every frame lasts exactly its delay.
captions: 20 frames, each one numbered in six blocks.
Readers: delay bytes, ffprobe, decoded pixels.

scenes.narration: One delay for all frames: nothing is lost. The mp4 rate is a hundred divided by the delay. Three gives thirty three point three three, not thirty. Every frame is kept, the length exact.

Now two, three, four, six, ten, repeated. The default mp4 is a hundred frames per second with a hundred frames: each frame repeated for its delay. Dash f p s underscore mode passthrough keeps twenty frames with exact times, but the file lasts point nine one seconds. The last delay is gone.
captions: passthrough: 20 frames, 0.91 s. The last delay is gone.

scenes.narration: Back to three hundredths. Dash r thirty drops nothing, but holds each frame thirty three milliseconds: eleven percent longer. Dash v f f p s equals thirty keeps point six seconds and drops frames five and fifteen. On the mix, both squeeze two, three and four hundredths into thirty three milliseconds.
captions: -r 30: 0.667 s, 11% longer. fps=30: frames 5 and 15 dropped.

scenes.narration: Without a rate flag, the delays survive. Force a rate, and you change the time. A delay of zero is read as ten hundredths. Not tested: browsers, other gif writers, real animations, other builds.
captions: No rate flag: the delays survive. Force a rate: the time changes.
Not tested: browsers, other writers, real animations.
